verdict.rationale: Superhuman documents several background automations: Auto Labels (including custom AI-prompt labels), Auto Archive, Auto Drafts and automatic follow-up reminders. One line also describes building agents that "run proactively based on triggers you set." However, that user-defined trigger/agent builder rests on a single thin claim with unclear scope, and the other automations are mostly preset toggles. missing for 10: detailed documentation of the trigger-based agent builder (available triggers, actions, scheduling), evidence that user-built automations can take actions such as sending without approval, and independent or hands-on corroboration that automations run reliably in the background.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Use chat or our visual builder to create agents that run proactively based on triggers you set and the work you connect.
Superhuman AI can automatically archive marketing, cold pitches, and social network updates. Turn on Auto Archive, and eliminate inbox clutter for good.
You can even make your own Auto Labels with short AI prompts like "job applications" or "requests to review work".
Get an email assistant that automatically labels incoming emails, archives low-priority messages, drafts replies, and reminds you to follow up.
Emails are labeled the moment they arrive, so you can see what's important and what's not.
